title.en: Relative velocity in a plane: rain and river problems

heading.en: Holding an umbrella on a bicycle

hook.en: On a still, rainy day the rain falls straight down, yet a cyclist has to tilt the umbrella forward. The faster she rides, the more she tilts it.

objectives.en: Find relative velocity as a vector difference
Find the least time and the shortest path to cross a river

narration.en: On a still, rainy day the rain falls straight down, yet a cyclist has to tilt the umbrella forward. The faster she rides, the more she tilts it.

title.en: Relative velocity is a vector difference

body.en: In two dimensions $\vec v_{BA} = \vec v_B - \vec v_A$: add $-\vec v_A$ to $\vec v_B$ by the triangle law. For rain falling at $v_r$ and a cyclist at $v_c$, the rain seems to come from the front at an angle θ to the vertical with $\tan\theta = v_c/v_r$, so the umbrella is tilted forward by θ.

points.en: Rain: tan θ = v_cyclist / v_rain, tilt forward
Magnitude √(v_r² + v_c²) when they are perpendicular

narration.en: In two dimensions $\vec v_{BA} = \vec v_B - \vec v_A$: add $-\vec v_A$ to $\vec v_B$ by the triangle law. For rain falling at $v_r$ and a cyclist at $v_c$, the rain seems to come from the front at an angle θ to the vertical with $\tan\theta = v_c/v_r$, so the umbrella is tilted forward by θ.

body.en: A boat moves at $v_b$ relative to the water; the water flows at $v_r$. Its velocity over the ground is the vector sum. Heading straight across gives the least time $t = d/v_b$ with drift $v_r d/v_b$. Heading upstream at θ with $\sin\theta = v_r/v_b$ gives the shortest path (straight across), taking $t = d/\sqrt{v_b^2 - v_r^2}$; this is possible only if $v_b > v_r$.

points.en: Shortest path: sin θ = v_r / v_b upstream

narration.en: A boat moves at $v_b$ relative to the water; the water flows at $v_r$. Its velocity over the ground is the vector sum. Heading straight across gives the least time $t = d/v_b$ with drift $v_r d/v_b$. Heading upstream at θ with $\sin\theta = v_r/v_b$ gives the shortest path (straight across), taking $t = d/\sqrt{v_b^2 - v_r^2}$; this is possible only if $v_b > v_r$.

title.en: Steer a boat across a river

narration.en: Choose the boat speed, the river speed and the heading. Press cross. The yellow track shows the path over the ground; the label shows how far downstream the boat lands.

caption.en: Set the boat's speed in still water, the river speed and the heading (degrees upstream from straight across). Press Cross and watch the drift.

tryThis.en: Head straight across (0°). Note the time and the drift.
With river 3 m/s and boat 5 m/s, find the heading that lands the boat directly opposite.
Make the river faster than the boat. Can you still land directly opposite?

say.en: Rain falls straight down at v r. The cyclist moves forward at v c.
Rain relative to the cyclist is v rain minus v cyclist: add the cyclist's velocity reversed.
The rain seems to come from the front, at theta to the vertical, with tan theta equal to v c over v r. Tilt the umbrella forward by theta.

problem.en: A river 400 m wide flows at 3 m/s. A boat moves at 5 m/s in still water. Find (a) the least crossing time and the drift, (b) the heading and time for the shortest path.

steps.en: (a) Head straight across: t = 400/5 = 80 s; drift = 3 × 80 = 240 m.
(b) sin θ = 3/5, so θ ≈ 37° upstream from straight across.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A river 400 m wide flows at 3 m/s. A boat moves at 5 m/s in still water. Find (a) the least crossing time and the drift, (b) the heading and time for the shortest path.

problem.en: Rain falls vertically at 4 m/s. A woman walks east at 3 m/s. Find the velocity of the rain relative to her.

steps.en: tan θ = 3/4 from the vertical: the rain seems to come from the east, in front of her.

answer.en: 5 m/s at tan⁻¹(3/4) ≈ 37° to the vertical, from the front

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Rain falls vertically at 4 m/s. A woman walks east at 3 m/s. Find the velocity of the rain relative to her.
The river flows at three metres per second and the boat moves at five. Choose the upstream heading that lands the boat directly opposite.

prompt.en: The river flows at 3 m/s and the boat moves at 5 m/s in still water. Choose the heading so the boat lands at the point directly opposite (drift 0). Lock in to cross.

explanation.en: sin θ = v_r / v_b = 3/5, so θ ≈ 37°. The upstream part of the boat's velocity cancels the river.

hint.en: The boat's upstream component v_b sin θ must equal the river speed.

body.en: Least time: point the boat straight across and let the river carry it. Shortest path: point it upstream so v_b sin θ = v_r. If v_r > v_b, no heading reaches the opposite point.

narration.en: Two river answers. Least time: point the boat straight across and let the river carry it. Shortest path: point it upstream so v_b sin θ = v_r. If v_r > v_b, no heading reaches the opposite point.

mnemonic.en: Time: straight across. Path: sine = river/boat.

points.en: In a plane, v_BA = v_B − v_A is found with vectors.
Rain–umbrella: tilt forward by θ with tan θ = v_c / v_r.
River: least time straight across (t = d/v_b); shortest path upstream with sin θ = v_r/v_b, t = d/√(v_b² − v_r²).

homework.en: A man can swim at 4 km/h in still water across a river 1 km wide flowing at 2 km/h. Find the time for the shortest path. (Answer: about 17.3 min)

narration.en: Recap. In a plane, v_BA = v_B − v_A is found with vectors. Rain–umbrella: tilt forward by θ with tan θ = v_c / v_r. River: least time straight across (t = d/v_b); shortest path upstream with sin θ = v_r/v_b, t = d/√(v_b² − v_r²).
